title: Software Development Costs & Exempt Organization Wind-Down

questions.q: For a tax year beginning in 2026, domestic software development costs are:

choices.A: Capitalized and amortized over five years
choices.D: Capitalized to the software and amortized over 15 years under §197

questions.why: OBBBA restored immediate expensing of domestic R&E for tax years beginning after 2024. Software development is statutorily treated as R&E under §174(c)(3) — this is a characterization rule, not an election. Foreign R&E is still 15-year.

questions.q: A company develops a mobile app that it sells to consumers through the App Store. For §41 purposes, the software is:

choices.A: Internal-use software, subject to the high threshold of innovation test
choices.B: Not internal-use software, so only the four-part test applies
choices.C: Ineligible because consumer apps are not technological in nature
choices.D: Dual-function software subject to the 25% safe harbor

questions.why: Software developed for sale, lease, or license to third parties is excluded from the internal-use software rules and therefore escapes the high threshold of innovation test entirely. This is the favorable posture for a commercial product portfolio.

questions.q: A development shop builds a website for a client under a fixed-fee contract. The client pays regardless of technical outcome and owns all deliverables. The developer's costs are:

choices.A: QREs eligible for the §41 credit at 100%
choices.C: Deductible, but NOT eligible for the credit — funded research

questions.why: Research funded by another person is excluded. The two tests are who bears the economic risk and who retains substantial rights. A fixed fee payable regardless of success plus IP assignment to the client fails both. The costs remain deductible; only the credit is lost.

questions.q: A company pays a domestic contractor $200,000 for qualified research, bearing the economic risk and retaining substantial rights. Compute the contract research QRE.
questions.why: 65% of qualifying contract research amounts. $200,000 x 0.65 = $130,000. The 75% rate applies only to qualified research consortia.

questions.q: An employee spends 85% of their time performing qualified research. For QRE purposes, the includible portion of their wages is:
questions.why: If substantially all (at least 80%) of an employee's services constitute qualified services, 100% of that employee's wages are a QRE. Below 80%, allocate actual qualified time.

questions.q: A founder personally writes all the code for a product but takes no salary. The wage QREs attributable to that work are:

choices.A: The fair market value of comparable engineering services
choices.C: 65% of imputed value, as contract research
choices.D: An amount elected by the taxpayer up to reasonable compensation

questions.why: Wage QREs require amounts actually paid that constitute wages. There is no imputation of uncompensated founder labor. This is the structural reason an uncompensated founder's R&D credit collapses to supplies plus 65% of contractors.

questions.q: Which cost is a QRE under §41?

choices.A: Cloud compute used to train and test models during development
choices.B: Production hosting for a released application
choices.C: IDE and GitHub subscriptions for the engineering team

questions.why: Payments for the right to use computers in the conduct of qualified research are QREs. Production hosting of a shipped product is not research. General developer tooling is ordinary §162 overhead — QRE supplies must be tangible property used and consumed in the research.

questions.q: A company had no QREs in any of the three preceding tax years. Under the Alternative Simplified Credit, the current-year credit rate is:

choices.A: 20% of QREs over a base amount
choices.B: 14% of QREs over 50% of the three-year average

questions.why: When there are no QREs in any of the three preceding years, the ASC is 6% of current-year QREs. Otherwise it is 14% of the excess over 50% of the prior three-year average.

questions.q: Work performed on a product AFTER it is functionally ready for commercial release is generally:

choices.A: Still a QRE because the product continues to improve
choices.B: Excluded as research after commercial production, unless it is a genuinely new component with its own uncertainty

questions.why: Research after commercial production begins is excluded. This makes the per-product release date the decisive fact for allocating a development year, and it is why the boundary must be recorded as it happens rather than reconstructed.

questions.q: A dissolving 501(c)(3) has $40,000 remaining after paying all liabilities. Those assets may be distributed to:

choices.A: The founding directors, in proportion to their service
choices.B: Another 501(c)(3) organization or a government entity
choices.D: The organization's largest donors, as a refund

questions.why: The organizational test requires a dissolution clause dedicating assets to exempt purposes. Distribution to insiders is private inurement, can retroactively jeopardize exempt status for open years, and exposes recipients to §4958 excess benefit excise taxes.

questions.q: A terminating public charity filing Form 990-EZ must attach which schedule reporting its asset distributions?
questions.why: Schedule N reports liquidation, termination, dissolution, or significant disposition of assets — asset by asset, with each recipient's name, address, and EIN, and whether any officer or director became an owner of the assets.

questions.q: An exempt organization fails to file a required annual return for three consecutive years. The consequence is:

choices.A: A penalty but no effect on status
choices.B: Automatic revocation of exempt status by operation of law

questions.why: Exempt status is revoked automatically on the filing due date of the third consecutive missed year. Reinstatement requires a new exemption application. Confirm an organization is not already auto-revoked before planning a dissolution.
